paragraphs: A powerful king, so the story goes, was out in the forest when he came upon a sage. After a short conversation he was so struck by the man's purity and wisdom that he wanted to give him a present.

The sage politely declined. The forest gave him fruit to eat, the mountain streams gave him clean water, tree bark served as clothing and the caves were his home. What did he need from the king, or from anyone?
The king kept pleading. Please accept something, he said, just so that I may be blessed, and come with me to my palace. At last the sage gave in and went along.

At the palace, before handing over the gift, the king sat down to pray. Lord, give me more children. Lord, give me more wealth. Lord, give me more land. Lord, make my body healthier. The list went on.

Before the king had finished, the sage rose and quietly walked out. The bewildered king ran after him, calling that he had not yet received his gifts. The sage turned and told him that he did not beg from beggars. The king, he said, was himself only a beggar, so what could he possibly give? He told the king to stop following him.
learn: If our prayers, or our relationships, are mostly a list of demands, we are beggars no matter how rich we look. Real devotion, like real friendship, gives without bargaining.
